policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere and ketiv differ only in the pointing/orthography of the preposition min before ha-se'arah; both read 'from the whirlwind'. ASV 'out of the whirlwind' renders either identically, and JOB.38.1 carries no mapped textual note, so nothing in the English distinguishes them. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

The readings differ only in the definite article on shachar (ha-shachar qere vs shachar ketiv). English supplies 'the' before 'dayspring' whether or not the Hebrew noun is articular, and ASV JOB.38.12 has no mapped textual note, so the wording does not distinguish the readings. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

ASV JOB.38.41 reads 'When his young ones cry unto God', a plural subject matching the qere yeladav ('his young ones'); the ketiv ילדו reads naturally as the singular yaldo, 'his child'. The plural of the ASV rendering distinguishes the qere, which the translators followed.
